labels.text: Operate on this repository instead of the current directory

S66.01.note: The code has a flag, not a picker. Expected says the user chooses before the session starts, which the flag does; /status does not print the folder, so the check is indirect.
steps: In a terminal, run agi --help and read the first lines about the -C / --repo option.
Run agi -C /path/to/another/repo from a different folder.
Ask the agent which folder it is in, or type /status and read the Account/Mode lines.
Compare: the session should work in the folder given to --repo, not the folder you started from.
S66.01.where: agi --repo <PATH> (short form: agi -C <PATH>), typed in the terminal before the session starts. There is no interactive repository picker in the code.

S66.03.note: Worktrees are a text list, not a picker. The create argument shape was read from the code and not run.
steps: Open agi in a git repository and type /worktree.
Read the list headed Git worktrees (N) with each branch and path.
Type /worktree create <name> to make a new worktree (argument form taken from the handler, not tried).
Type /worktree and check the new worktree appears in the list.
S66.03.where: /worktree (also /wt) typed in the coding session; subcommands create, add, new, remove, rm, exit are handled in the same command.

S66.05.note: Archived sessions are left out of the list. The key that opens a row was not confirmed.
steps: Open agi and type /sessions.
Read the list: each row shows an 8-character id, a date and time, a message count and the title.
Pick one row and confirm to open it (the key for opening was not checked in code).
Compare: the list should show your saved sessions, and the chosen one should open.
S66.05.where: /sessions (also /history, or /resume with no argument) typed in the coding session.

S66.06.note: Rename is typed, not clicked. The session list shows titles only when one is set.
steps: Open /sessions and note a session id.
Type /rename <id> <new title> with that id and a new name.
Read the reply: it should say Renamed session with the id and the new title.
Type /sessions again and check the new title is shown on that row.
S66.06.where: /rename <id> <new title> typed in the coding session; the title shows in the /sessions list.

S66.07.needs: a session that asks for a tool approval
S66.07.note: Only the waiting-for-approval state has a visible label. Running, idle, failed and closed are not shown as words in the session list, so this item is only partly present.
steps: Open agi in a folder and send a request that needs a tool approval, such as a shell command.
Watch the status line above the prompt while the approval box is open.
Compare: it should say Waiting for your approval.
Look at /sessions for any other status words; none were found in the code.
S66.07.where: The status line above the prompt shows Waiting for your approval while a tool approval is pending. No visible running, idle, failed or closed label was found in the code.

S66.09.note: The popup header is Files, found in the widget. Enter behaviour was read from the module comment, not run.
steps: Open agi in a project folder.
Type @ in the message box.
Type part of a file name, such as the start of a file you know exists.
Compare: a popup titled Files should list matching files, and Enter should put the chosen path in the message.
S66.09.where: Type @ in the message box to open the file picker, then type part of a file name.

S66.13.needs: a project folder with a file
S66.13.note: There is no text-selection feature in the code. The line-range mention is the closest match, and it is typed, not selected with the mouse.
steps: Open agi in a project folder.
Type @ and a file path, then #L10-20 after it.
Send a message such as explain this code.
Compare: the agent should receive only the lines in that range as context.
S66.13.where: Type @ followed by a file path and #L with a line range (for example @path/file.rs#L10-20) in the message box.

S66.15.note: No separate terminal panel was found. Output goes into the conversation transcript, and no visible label text was found to quote.
steps: Open agi in a project folder.
Type !ls and press Enter.
Read the output that appears in the conversation above the prompt.
Compare: the command output should appear in the session.
S66.15.where: Type ! followed by a shell command in the message box, such as !ls.

S66.17.note: Searched for command history and exit status labels in apps/cli. Found only the /history session picker (which is not a command history) and tool timings in the transcript. No view that lists commands with their exit status was found.

S66.18.needs: a git repository with changed files
S66.18.note: /diff only prints a text summary, not the line-level view. The arrow-key movement is taken from the widget header comment.
steps: In a git repository with changes, open agi and type /diff-review.
Read the list of changed files gathered from git status.
Move to a file with the arrow keys and read its line-level diff.
Compare: the diff should show the lines the agent changed.
S66.18.where: /diff-review typed in the coding session (a line-level view opens for changed files).

S66.19.needs: a git repository with changed files
S66.19.note: The summary is generated by git.rs; whether it labels created or deleted files was not confirmed from the code.
steps: In a git repository with changes, open agi and type /diff.
Read the summary of changed files it prints.
Compare: the summary should list the files that the session changed.
Check whether created and deleted files are marked as such in the summary.
S66.19.where: /diff typed in the coding session (prints a summary of changed files).

S66.21.needs: a git repository with agent changes
S66.21.note: The widget header says y/n/s decide the hunk shown, but the list is per file, and the effect on the working tree was not run.
steps: Type /diff-review in a repository with agent changes.
Select a change and press y to approve it, n to reject it, or s to skip it.
Read the label that appears: [y] Approved, [n] Rejected or [s] Skipped.
Compare: the decision should be recorded for that change; reject should remove it from the working tree.
S66.21.where: /diff-review, then press y, n or s on each file or hunk shown.

labels.text: (no checkpoints yet: each prompt you send makes one)

S66.22.needs: a session with at least one prompt sent
S66.22.note: The list is the checkpoint picker; the summaries come from history.rs.
steps: Send a prompt to the agent so a checkpoint is made.
Type /rewind with no other words.
Read the list of checkpoints.
Compare: each prompt should show as a checkpoint; with none yet, the message says no checkpoints yet.
S66.22.where: /rewind typed with no argument in the coding session opens the checkpoint list.

S66.23.needs: a git repository and at least two prompts
S66.23.note: Options shown depend on whether the checkpoint has code files and a conversation. The restore result message was not run.
steps: Send two prompts in a repository so two checkpoints exist.
Type /rewind and pick the first checkpoint.
Choose Restore code and conversation.
Compare: the files and the conversation should go back to that checkpoint, and the screen should say what was restored.
S66.23.where: /rewind, pick a checkpoint, then choose Restore code and conversation (or Restore conversation, or Restore code).

labels.text: read-only tools only, no file edits. The model plans before acting.

S66.24.note: The mode description says read-only tools and no file edits, which matches Expected.
steps: Open agi and type /plan.
Look at the mode badge in the status bar: it should say Plan.
Ask for a change to a file and check the agent proposes a plan without editing.
Type /plan accept to approve the plan, then compare that edits are now allowed.
S66.24.where: /plan in the coding session, or press Shift+Tab until the mode shows Plan.

labels.text: file edits, read-only tools and commands the safety classifier clears run; everything else asks. /auto-mode-setup reviews this repository.

S66.25.note: The code has no mode named edit or agent. Auto is the closest match, and it is the edit-without-asking mode.
steps: Open agi and press Shift+Tab until the mode badge says Auto.
Read the mode description: file edits run, and everything else asks.
Ask the agent to edit a file.
Compare: the edit should run without asking, while a command should still ask.
S66.25.where: Shift+Tab until the mode shows Auto (the edit mode).

S66.26.needs: none (Bypass and FullAuto appear only if the session was started with them allowed)
S66.26.note: Expected uses ask every time, auto-approve safe and autonomous. Bypass and FullAuto are only offered when the session allows them.
steps: Open agi and read the mode badge (Default at start).
Press Shift+Tab to step through the modes: Default, Plan, Auto, Bypass, FullAuto.
Ask for a file edit or a command in Default and check it asks first.
Compare: in Auto, edits run; in Bypass or FullAuto, prompts are skipped, so no approval box appears.
S66.26.where: Shift+Tab (Cycle permission mode) in the coding session.

S66.27.note: The status bar ctx indicator was found but its exact wording was not confirmed.
steps: Open agi and send a few messages.
Type /status.
Read the line that starts with Context:.
Compare: the percentage should grow as the conversation gets longer.
S66.27.where: /status (or /context, /ctx) typed in the coding session; the status bar also has a ctx indicator.

S66.28.needs: a session with at least one message
S66.28.note: /usage was found but its output was not read, so plan usage on screen is unconfirmed.
steps: Send a message to the agent.
Type /cost.
Read the Turns line and the cost line that follows.
Compare: turns and money spent should match what you sent; /usage shows plan usage.

S66.29.note: The exact state words in the /tasks list were not read.
steps: Start a long background task, for example with /bg or /background.
Type /tasks.
Read the list of tasks and their state.
Type /tasks show <id> for one task and compare with Expected.
S66.29.where: /tasks typed in the coding session (also /tasks show <id>, /tasks stop <id>).

labels.text: Use ←/→ to switch to Running or Library tabs.

S66.30.note: The tab shows the running list; the result of each subagent was not checked in the code.
steps: Start a task that uses subagents.
Type /agents.
Press the Right arrow to switch to the Running tab.
Compare: the tab should list the running subagents under Running subagents.
S66.30.where: /agents typed in the coding session, then the Running tab.

S66.39.needs: a session with some work done
S66.39.note: The recap is a prompt sent to the model, so its layout is not fixed in code; the prompt asks for goals, decisions, files changed, tests run, risks and next actions.
steps: Do some work in a session, such as an edit and a command.
Type /recap.
Wait for the answer.
Compare: the recap should cover goals, decisions, files changed, checks run and next steps.

labels.text: This conversation continued in another app, so it now shows the saved version and your message continues from there.
Continue previous session, from this device or from your account.

S66.41.needs: the desktop app installed, or a signed-in account for the cloud
S66.41.note: Continuing in a phone or editor was not confirmed in the code; the desktop and cloud routes were found.
steps: In the coding session, type /desktop and open the desktop app.
Check the session continues there with the same history.
Or type /continue-with-cloud and read the reply.
Compare: the session should continue in the other client and the message should say it continued in another app.
S66.41.where: /desktop (or /app) to continue in the desktop app; /continue-with-cloud to move it to the cloud; agi resume in the terminal to pick it up again.
